title: startplasma reads "LANG" at the wrong moment in time, leading to a wrong value for "LANG" on a multi-locale system
line: On first login, Plasma now uses the user's own locale instead of the system locale the login screen started it with.
explanation: When plasma-localerc had no LANG, startplasma saved its own process LANG there on first login. SDDM starts the session with a cleaned environment holding only the system LANG from /etc/locale.conf, so on systems with a different user locale (from environment.d) the system locale was saved and then pushed to systemd and every app. Now, when no LANG is saved yet, startplasma takes LANG from the systemd user environment if it has one, and only falls back to its own LANG otherwise.

commits.message:
startkde: take the first LANG from the systemd user environment

Display managers like SDDM can start the session with the system LANG,
so on first login that value was saved to plasma-localerc instead of the
user locale from environment.d. Prefer systemd's LANG when one is set.

BUG: 497501

media.caption: First login with systemd --user LANG=en_GB.UTF-8 and startplasma started with LANG=C.UTF-8: C.UTF-8 is saved and overrides the user locale everywhere
Same first login with the fix: en_GB.UTF-8 is saved and used by systemd and plasmashell

review.text: Preferring the systemd user manager's LANG fixes SDDM + environment.d, but the manager's LANG defaults to the system locale from /etc/locale.conf. Display managers that set a per-user LANG (LightDM/GDM via AccountsService) start startplasma with the user's choice, which this change would now replace with the system locale on first login, the same bug in reverse. The tester's own regression note shows the fallback to locale.conf's en_US.
changes: Only take systemd's LANG when it actually differs from the system default (e.g. it was set by environment.d, not inherited from /etc/locale.conf), otherwise keep the LANG the display manager passed.
Test first login with a per-user LANG passed by the display manager and no environment.d LANG, and confirm it is kept.
